Requirement on the board: Read five key groups on lines shared with the indicator cathodes, plus three separate contact inputs elsewhere in the machine
Voltage domain: 3V3 or 5V (switch only pulls low so either works)
Electrical detail: Five panel lines are BIDIRECTIONAL: each sinks its group's indicator current and is then read as an input once the anode rail is blanked. The panel puts 1 kohm in series with each key pair, so the board's own pull-up sets the closed-key level - 1 kohm against 1 kohm gives about 2.5 V on a 5 V part, which works but is not generous; prefer a weaker pull-up. The other three inputs (tank level, hot water knob, steam knob) are plain contacts on their own wires
Suggested placement: Panel breakout preferred - collapses the panel's share of these inputs onto a few conductors. Note the two knob microswitches and the tank reed are not on the panel and reach the board on their own wires
Serves: S1-S5 pushbuttons + S7/S8 knob microswitches + S6 tank level reed
Status: Traced on the physical panel board. The count is 8 signals: 5 key groups (ten switches in parallel pairs) plus 3 elsewhere. See docs/connector-pinouts.md

Requirement on the board: Sink indicator current on the shared key lines, and gate their common anode rail
Controller resource: Shares E1 lines; plus one timer output for the rail
Electrical detail: ~10-15 mA per element through the panel's ~300 ohm series resistors, which are on the panel and stay with it; the anode rail must carry every lit element at once. Indicators cost no pin beyond E1's five - each group's cathodes share the line carrying its key. The sixth function the circuit diagram draws, WATER, is on the gauge assembly and is E18, not here
Serves: 8 indicator elements across 5 functions on the button panel (PWR MAN ONE TWO PRG)
Status: ONE timer output serves the panel, not eight. The rail gate is the multiplexing gate: it must be blanked to read the keys, and modulating it is how brightness varies - globally, not per element. Confirm by watching whether two lit indicators ramp together. See docs/connector-pinouts.md

Requirement on the board: Drive two gauge movements through the driver already on the gauge assembly
Controller resource: 2 timer outputs (step clocks) + 3 GPIO (two direction lines, one reset)
Electrical detail: The VID66-08 sits on the gauge assembly, not the main board, so a retained board means the driver is INHERITED and the controller drives logic lines rather than motor phases. Step clocks need timer channels - a needle has inertia and an uneven rate reads as stutter. Board supply is 5 V so the driver's inputs are probably 5 V CMOS; a 3.3 V controller may not clear Vih, which is a level-shift question on five lines. Step size, phase current and gearing NOT ESTABLISHED, though steps-per-sweep is obtainable by counting between the end stops
Suggested placement: Gauge assembly - the driver is already there and stays with it; the main board supplies logic lines only
Serves: MOT1 espresso resistance-to-pour gauge; MOT2 milk temperature gauge
Status: Inferred, not traced: the part is absent from main-board spare photos and the 9-conductor harness only closes if the driver is local. Retaining an out-of-production driver is an obtainability risk, distinct from the unknown-condition question OBL-PHYSICAL-CONFIGURATION-001.C3 asks. Both movements have end stops and the machine homes against them at power-on; a replacement owes the same routine. See docs/connector-pinouts.md

Requirement on the board: Drive the panel buzzer through a transistor
Electrical detail: Magnetic vs piezo NOT ESTABLISHED - a magnetic sounder needs a drive waveform, a self-drive piezo needs only on/off
Status: Now enumerated; was absent from the channel enumeration

Group: Temperature front end - Option A (NTCs retained)
Requirement on the board: Convert three resistive sensors against a stable reference
Electrical detail: 100k NTC against 10k 0.1% divider with ~100nF filtering (OEM used 1%). Ratiometric or precision Vref required. Divider sensitivity peaks near 85-90 degC, which is where the brew band sits
Serves: Coffee block / steam block / steam wand sensors
Status: Established from OEM sheet 3-3; mutually exclusive with E6

Controller resource: SPI bus + 1 chip select per converter
Electrical detail: MAX31865 is single-channel so three are needed: 3 shared bus pins + 3 CS, optional DRDY per chip (poll instead to save 3 pins). One 4.3k 0.1% low-tempco Rref per chip - this part sets the accuracy. Alternative: one multi-channel delta-sigma with excitation (ADS124S06/S08 class) does all three on 1 bus + 1 CS with a single Rref
Suggested placement: Sensor breakout - keeps converters near the leads and away from mains switching; lets the sensing option change without respinning the main board
Status: Proposed; mutually exclusive with E5. PT1000 (not PT100) is what makes the fitted 2-wire leads viable - ~0.26 degC per ohm of lead vs ~2.6

Electrical detail: Typical ratiometric output is 0.5-4.5 V on a 5 V supply, so the board must provide a 5 V excitation rail and either a 5V-tolerant ADC or a divider to 3V3. Ratiometric reference preferred so supply drift cancels
Status: Parts NOT SELECTED for either path

Electrical detail: OEM fits a 2k pull-up to 5V, which implies an open-drain output. If open-drain, re-reference by pulling up to 3V3 - no level shifter. If push-pull, a divider or shifter is required. Open-drain vs push-pull NOT ESTABLISHED
Serves: Flow meter on the coffee pump suction line
Status: Type confirmed digital; drive style and K-factor (pulses/litre) both open

Requirement on the board: Present both crossings of every mains cycle to an interrupt
Electrical detail: Requires a NEW front end - the fitted circuit is half-wave (series 1N4007) and gives one crossing per cycle. Propagation delay must be low and repeatable: the phase offset between true crossing and detected edge is bounded by no declared figure and must not be invented
Suggested placement: Power/mains board with isolated output to logic
Serves: Half-cycle actuation timing reference for heaters and pumps

Requirement on the board: Command each element on or off every supply half-cycle
Controller resource: GPIO out into an isolated gate driver
Electrical detail: Elements were measured at 52.7 and 47.0 ohm cold, giving 1004 W and 1126 W at 230 V - about 4.4 A and 4.9 A, ~9.3 A together. Use those figures, not the 1000 W circuit-diagram label they supersede. Size a ZERO-CROSSING optotriac (MOC3063 class) into a triac rated well above 4.9 A after derating, with heatsink - or an external SSR. Mechanical relays are excluded because they cannot be commanded within a half-cycle. The OEM Z0409NF at 4 A is a pump-class part and is NOT adequate here
Suggested placement: Power/mains board - physically separated from logic
Status: Replacement required. Both heaters together draw ~9.3 A, which is the constraint REQ-POWER-BUDGET-001 and OBL-ELECTRICAL-THERMAL-SAFETY-001.C3 arbitrate against an ordinary 10 A domestic circuit. The machine's 5 A fuse protects the control supply and is NOT in series with the elements, so it enforces nothing about heater exclusivity

Requirement on the board: Modulate each pump timed against the zero-cross reference
Controller resource: GPIO out into an isolated gate driver
Electrical detail: Driver MUST remain RANDOM-PHASE (MOC3021 class) - a zero-crossing optotriac cannot phase-control. Load is Ulka class at roughly 0.25 A each, so the OEM Z0409NF triac is adequate. Snubber required
Status: Arrangement retained; device class confirmed phase-capable from OEM sheet 3-2

Controller resource: GPIO out into a mains-rated switching device
Electrical detail: Coils are MAINS AC - confirmed from the OEM sheet, which switches them with 12 V relays. Coil current NOT ESTABLISHED. Inductive load, so a snubber is required whichever device is used. If relays are retained the board also needs a 12 V coil rail
Status: Coil class established; coil current not

Requirement on the board: Confirm mains is actually present at each heater node
Electrical detail: OEM uses an AC-input optocoupler (LTV814) fed through 120k 1W. Detects a relay that did not close, a welded contact, or an open thermal cutout - this is actuation confirmation, not a nicety
Suggested placement: Power/mains board with isolated output to logic
Status: Now enumerated; was absent from the channel enumeration

Controller resource: UART (2 pins) or direct panel drive
Electrical detail: Conservative figure is direct drive. The OEM CMDTX/SLVOK pair is not an inter-board link at all - both microcontrollers sit on the main board - so the panel board is retained as a passive assembly and carries no controller to speak to and no proprietary framing to reverse-engineer. A display is a separate question this row does not settle
Status: Undecided; the retained-panel alternative no longer arises

Requirement on the board: Sink the indicator's cathode on the gauge assembly
Voltage domain: 5V, on a supply local to the gauge assembly
Electrical detail: Switched rather than modulated: its anode ties to a supply on the gauge assembly, not to the button panel's gated rail - run with a low tank it holds steady while the PWR element ramps. That separation is what frees the ninth conductor of the gauge harness
Serves: The visual half of low-water annunciation; the buzzer is the audible half
Status: Fitted, observed running. Was carried by no document and no node. Keeping one half of the annunciation and dropping the other degrades it without removing it. See docs/connector-pinouts.md

Requirement on the board: Carry signals across each partition boundary
Electrical detail: Panel breakout: any low pin-count bus (SPI/I2C/UART) will do and collapses the button/LED/stepper harness. Power board: the boundary is the mains isolation barrier - either the isolated gate drives themselves carry it, or a digital isolator does
Isolation: REINFORCED on the power-board boundary only
Status: Follows from the placement column - not itself decided

Requirement on the board: Supply every rail the above needs from mains
Voltage domain: 3V3 logic, 5V sensors and indicators, 12V if any relay coils are retained
Electrical detail: Budget >=10 W with headroom. Rough draw: MCU ~0.35 W, indicators ~0.75 W, steppers ~2 W (unestablished), opto drives ~0.5 W, sensors ~0.1 W, display unknown. The OEM supply is a 9 V 2.5 VA transformer and is nowhere near adequate

Requirement on the board: Keep the analogue front ends quiet
Electrical detail: Separate analogue ground and reference for E5/E6/E7, returned away from mains switching currents. This is what the accuracy figures in the channel enumeration assume and nothing else guarantees
